title: Sustainable development
reading: The UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) are a common plan for sustainable development in the whole world. Their goal is to eradicate poverty, combat different types of inequality and stop climate change by 2030.

The weather and the climate are not the same thing. The weather is what we see every day when we are outside or look out of the window, while the climate is the average weather measured over a long period. Over the past 100 years, major changes have taken place in the earth’s climate. Most of the world’s climate researchers believe that human CO2 emissions are behind the rapid and far-reaching changes we see today.
Renewable resources is a term that describes self-renewing natural resources. People can draw on these resources, and if exploited properly, they are not used up.

Locally produced food is produced near the consumer When food is produced locally, there is less need for transport and we thus save a lot of greenhouse gas emissions. It is also easier to control the production of locally produced food. This may concern crop sprays, the use of antibiotics in the meat and fish industry and animal welfare conditions.
discussion: Talk together Talk about climate change. How is it affecting your home country? How is it affecting Norway? Talk about renewable resources. What happens when people use these resources up more quickly than the rate at which nature is able to renew them? Talk about the advantages and disadvantages of locally produced food. Is it important for a country to be self-sufficient? Why or why not? Talk about the UN SDGs. Do you think some of them are more important than others? Does the whole world agree on this plan? exercises: Select the right answer What is the climate? The weather we see every day when we look out of the window. The average of the weather measured over a long period. Select the right answer What do most climate researchers believe is behind the rapid and far-reaching changes we see today? Natural changes. Human CO2 emissions. Most climate researchers don’t believe that the climate is undergoing rapid and far-reaching changes Select the right answer What is a renewable resource? Natural resources that are self-renewing and aren't used up if used correctly. Natural resources that are used up. A collective term for natural resources that can be used up and natural resources that aren’t used up if used correctly. Select right or wrong Read the statements. What is right? What is wrong? The earth’s temperature is not rising. Right Wrong The UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) are a common plan for sustainable development in the whole world. Right Wrong Climate and weather mean the same thing. Right Wrong One of the climate changes we are experiencing is that the ice is melting. Right Wrong Most climate researchers believe that climate change is man-made. Right Wrong Select right or wrong Read the statements. What is right? What is wrong? Sunshine, trees and wind are non-renewable resources. Right Wrong Oil is a non-renewable resource. Right Wrong Water is a renewable resource. Right Wrong When food is produced locally, there is less need for transport and we thus save greenhouse gas emissions. Right Wrong It is more difficult to control the production of locally produced food than food produced elsewhere. Right Wrong Click on the right image Which image shows a non-renewable resource?
teacher_notes: Lærerinnhold Tips til undervisningen Se filmen Filmen viser 21 klipp. I de første ti klippene ser vi miljøproblemene vi står ovenfor: is som smelter, røyk og forurensning, biltrafikk, flytrafikk, brennende skog, forsøpling og isbjørner som står alene på et isflak. De neste to klippene viser miljøvennlig energi: vannkraft og vindkraft. De siste ni klippene viser hva vi som privatpersoner kan gjøre for å bekjempe klimakrisen: dyrke planter og grønnsaker, demonstrere for klimavennlige tiltak, sykle til jobben, ta toget, bruke el-bil, pante flasker, kjøpe brukte klær og reparere klærne vi allerede har. Forslag til spørsmål Hva tenker du på når du hører ordet «bærekraftig»? Hva kan man gjøre for å leve bærekraftig? Hva burde man ikke gjøre? Er det enkelt å leve bærekraftig? Hvorfor? Hvorfor ikke? Hvem kan legge til rette for at mennesker skal kunne leve bærekraftig? Hvordan? Hvilke råd ville du gitt til en venn som ønsket å være mer miljøvennlig, men ikke visste hvordan? Snakk sammen Læreren kan gjerne samle på og presentere ulike nyhetsoppslag om naturkatastrofer som flom, tørke, skogbranner, ekstrem hete osv. rundt i verden. Under koronapandemien har vi sett at det er en fordel for et land å være selvforsynt med matvarer og også andre varer. Er det mulig for alle land å være like selvforsynte? Hva ville skjedd i Norge dersom vi bare kunne kjøpt mat og varer produsert i Norge?
